messages.subject: Re: colour=Group affects geom_errorbar & geom_errorbarh
parts:
On 8/21/2012 9:33 AM, Sante Kotturi wrote:
> I am plotting a heart rate response curve between two groups at 5 time
> points. The data came from a wide csv file that was converted using melt()
> and then summarized using summarizeSE()
>
> Problem: Everything works when I have colour=Group as in:
> ggplot(dfc2, aes(x=variable, y=value, colour=Group)) + geom_errorbar(...)
> + geom_errorbarh(....) + geom_line(...) + geom_point(...)
> However, when I remove the colour=Group:
> ggplot(dfc2, aes(x=variable, y=value) + geom_errorbar(...)
> + geom_errorbarh(....) + geom_line(...) + geom_point(...)
>
> Errors I'm getting:
> 1) horizontal error bars are much longer than before (literally extend off
> the graph)
> 2) vertical error bars no longer follow the position dodge
>
> Notes:
> 1) I am using a position_dodge(0.1) which works with colour defined.
> 2) Because the 5 time points represent unequal times (some were sampled
> over 10 minutes, others 30) the horizontal error bars are there to
> represent the amount of time sampled over, not actual error bars.. there
> values did not change however when removing the colour definition.
> 3) I'm using ggplot() + geom_errobar() + geom_errorbarh() + geom_line() +
> geom_point() + scale_shape_manual() + scale_color_hue() +
> scale_y_continuous() + scale_x_discrete()

Not having example data, I'm just guessing.

When you set colour=Group, that changes the default grouping of the data
to include Group. This grouping affects how summary statistics are made
and how dodging is performed. You can override the default grouping by
setting group=Group. This will not change colors, but will make things
be grouped the same was when you had colour=Group.


--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
